events.summary:
At 817 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Up to 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Lincoln County.

Low water crossings along Gallo Arroyo and Hasperos Canyon Arroyo may
be impacted.

events.region: Howell, MO; Oregon, MO; Shannon, MO
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Missouri, including the
following counties, Howell, Oregon and Shannon.

* WHEN...Until 200 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 900 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- This includes the following low water crossings...
Mahans Creek at County Road 501, Sycamore Creek at Highway H,
Thomas Hollow at Highway H, Rocky Creek at Highway H, Little
Rocky Creek at Highway H and Pine Hollow at Highway E.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winona, Birch Tree, Eminence, Montier, Alley Spring, West
Eminence, Teresita and Ozark National Scenic Riverways.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: North Laramie Valley/Shirley Basin; Ferris/Seminoe/Shirley Mountains; Central and West Carbon; Upper North Platte River Basin; Snowy Range/Medicine Bow NF; North Snowy Range Foothills
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 420 through 422 and fire
weather zones 425 through 427.

* WIND...During the daytime hours, west winds from 15 to 25 mph
with gusts up to 40 mph. Overnight, lighter southwest winds
of 5 to 15 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Daytime minimum RH between 5 and 10 percent on Saturday,
and between 10 and 15 percent on Sunday. Overnight recoveries
of 20 to 35 percent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Isolated high-based showers will have the
potential to produce gusty and erratic winds along with a few
strikes of lightning without much, if any, rainfall during the
afternoon and evening hours both Saturday and Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
